4th Period.workingNow: Learning what should and shouldn't ever be typed into an AI system, and how it stores what you tell it.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A persuasive 'How I Think We Should Use AI' article live on your portfolio site — your argued position on the best way to use AI, backed by this week's research, plus at least one image — pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can identify what information is safe or unsafe to give an AI tool, and explain how AI systems store and reuse what we tell them, so that I can protect my own and others' privacy online.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.NI.5 — Explain potential security threats and security measures to mitigate threats.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Log in & warm-up: one thing you'd never post online (3 min)
Quick overview: today's plan — no AI chat today (2 min)
I do: how AI stores & reuses what you type in (8 min)
We do: sort real examples — safe vs. never-share (10 min)
You do: write your own 3 never-share rules (5 min)
Exit Ticket: one thing that surprised you (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday's plan had you chatting directly with SchoolAI — we're pausing that this week to look underneath the hood first. Today you learn what actually happens to the words you type into an AI, so tomorrow's research digs into the bigger risks and benefits before you argue your own position on Friday.

6th Period.workingNow: Picking two aesthetics — feelings — you want your game to give players, and explaining why.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: MDA framework notes (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) + a one-page Game Design Plan for your SchoolAI game, shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can name the aesthetic — the feeling — I want my game to give players so that my design choices have a clear purpose.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: I do: what feeling should players have? (6 min)
We do: name a shared game's aesthetic as a class (6 min)
You do: pick 2 aesthetics for your game & explain why (12 min)
Exit Ticket: your game's one-word feeling (2 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday you listed mechanics — the rules and pieces. Today's the easy one: what should your game actually feel like to play? Tomorrow's the hard part — figuring out how those rules create that feeling.
